Druk Green Power Corp Ltd Insolvency Disrupts Bhutan’s Electricity Sector

Thimphu, June 27 – Druk Green Power Corp Ltd, a leading player in Bhutan’s electric utilities industry, has entered insolvency proceedings, sending shockwaves through the nation’s energy market and raising concerns over supply stability and employment.

The company, which operates several of Bhutan’s key hydropower plants, initiated insolvency procedures earlier this week following months of financial strain attributed to mounting operational costs and delayed payments from major clients. As administrators assess the firm’s assets and liabilities, day-to-day operations have already been affected.

“Several of our ongoing maintenance projects have been put on hold pending further instructions from the administrators,” said a senior operations manager at Druk Green Power Corp Ltd, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “We are doing our best to maintain essential services, but uncertainty remains high among staff.”

The company employs over 1,500 people across multiple sites. According to the Bhutanese Hydropower Workers’ Union, employees are anxious about their job security. “We urge the administrators to prioritize worker protections and ensure the continuity of critical infrastructure,” said union leader Sangay Dorji.

Industry analysts warn that the insolvency could disrupt electricity distribution, especially in rural areas. “Bhutan’s reliance on hydropower means any operational disruption has ripple effects throughout the economy,” noted Kinley Wangchuk, an energy sector consultant. “If the insolvency leads to a prolonged shutdown, it could impact both domestic supply and export commitments.”

The Bhutan Chamber of Commerce and Industry expressed hope for a swift resolution. “We are monitoring the situation closely and urge all stakeholders to work towards stability,” said a spokesperson. The administration process is ongoing, with further updates expected in the coming days.
